entry.title: Recognized in the World's Top 2% Scientists List
entry.summary: A note on my TopSciNet profile in the Stanford Top 2% Scientists single-year records.
entry.content:
I am pleased to share that my researcher profile appears in the Stanford Top 2% Scientists single-year records listed by TopSciNet. The profile identifies my affiliation with the Industrial University of Ho Chi Minh City and connects my work with Information and Communication Technologies, Artificial Intelligence and Image Processing, and Business and Management.

The Top 2% list uses citation-based indicators to identify researchers whose work has received notable scholarly attention within their fields. These indicators offer one way to understand research influence, but they cannot capture every dimension of scholarship, including teaching, practical impact, or the contributions of collaborators.

The profile’s latest visible single-year record is for 2025. It reports a rank of 4,127 among 458,615 researchers in Artificial Intelligence and Image Processing, with self-citations excluded. This is a 2025 figure and should not be confused with the 2019 year in the profile link.

I am grateful to the colleagues, students, and research partners whose ideas and collaboration have shaped this work. Recognition is an encouragement to keep asking useful questions and to pursue research that contributes to both scholarship and practice.

View my TopSciNet profile.

entry.title: You only live once, but if you do it right, once is enough
entry.summary: A short note on choices, responsibility, and staying strong when the road is hard.
entry.content:
There are many ways to live in this world, and it is up to each person to choose how to live. We cannot predict the future; all that matters is what is happening right now. Do not be too worried about your choice, because whether it produces the result you expect will be decided by your effort.

In life, there are many opportunities. There is no such thing as a good or a wrong choice, because each option leads to a different set of options. The path you are on is the consequence of a great many decisions.

When you take responsibility for your acts, and face the consequences of your choices, you are mature. Always be willing to admit and to correct your mistakes. Remember that you own your life, and that the only way for each of us to find our own worth is to live it. Let no one direct your life; follow where your heart leads instead.

Life is not as easy and as bright as it looks in films and novels. Real life is a mixture of light and dark. Many obstacles stand on the road to the top, and they serve to discourage us. Do not give up too quickly, because the road to success is paved with flowers and with hurdles that you must overcome. However bad things become, stay strong. Behind those difficulties, God has prepared a gift for us.

entry.title: You'll never walk alone
entry.summary: On the song by Rodgers and Hammerstein: keep your head up through the storm.
entry.content:
This world is filled with intrinsic risks, including the potential perils of insecurity. People feel thrilled and inspired when they listen to “You’ll Never Walk Alone”. When you are going through a storm, keep your head up and do not be afraid of the dark night ahead. After the storm there is a bright sky and the sweet silver song of a lark. Walk on through the wind, through the rain, through the hopes that have been thrown away. Walk on with hope in your heart, and you will never walk alone.

When you walk through a storm
Hold your head up high
And don’t be afraid of the dark
At the end of a storm
There’s a golden sky

The words are by Oscar Hammerstein II, with music by Richard Rodgers, for the musical Carousel. The best known recording is by Gerry and the Pacemakers. Listen to it on YouTube.
